featured_reviews.name: rajesh jaiswar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kari Apla is one of those rare restaurants that immediately makes you feel at home the moment you step inside. It’s a small, warm space in Khar with a simple, earthy charm — the kind of place where you can actually hear conversations, enjoy the aroma from the open kitchen, and feel connected to the food being prepared.

The menu is a beautiful mix of coastal, Kerala, and Maharashtrian flavours, but presented in a very thoughtful and modern way. Every dish has a story, and you can sense the amount of care the chefs put into balancing comfort with creativity. The curries are rich without being heavy, the spices are well-rounded, and the seafood is exceptionally fresh. Even the vegetarian dishes stand out with bold, homely flavours.

Their weekend brunch is especially worth trying — soft appams, dosas, light stews, filter coffee — everything tastes like a regional home kitchen brought into a modern dining space. Portions are satisfying and plating is elegant without being overdone.

Service is polite, patient, and genuinely interested in helping you choose. Because the space is compact, the whole experience feels personal and relaxed rather than rushed or commercial.

Prices are on the higher side, but completely justified considering the quality, originality, and the chef-driven approach. It’s not a “quick meal” type of place — it’s somewhere you go to slow down and enjoy food with intention.

Overall: Kari Apla is a wonderful blend of nostalgia, regional flavours, and modern presentation. If you enjoy coastal Indian cuisine or simply love trying thoughtfully crafted food, this is a spot you shouldn’t miss.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Locomo Express Hostel recommended Khoa Piyo Restaurant, and I visited there alone for dinner.

I asked for Kingfisher Ultra, and the manager initially confirmed that it was available. However, after a few minutes, another staff member came and informed me that it was not available and that only other brands were in stock. I then requested Budweiser, which was served.

The beer was served without any complimentary snacks like nuts or chips. I also had to ask separately for drinking water, whereas normally water is brought to the table automatically for customers.

I ordered chicken biryani, which was just okay.

After finishing my meal, I requested the bill, and the brought the QR code for payment. However, the manager took the bill from my hand with visible irritation, which felt uncomfortable and unprofessional.

When I was leaving, no staff member was present at the door to open it or even acknowledge me. Two staff members were sitting near the entrance, talking to each other, but there was no courtesy, greeting, or farewell shown.

Overall, I felt the service lacked basic hospitality, professionalism, and customer respect. I hope the management will take this feedback positively and improve their service standards.

featured_reviews.name: Danish Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Toooo Goooddd!!! This place offers so many cuisines that your mind will be confused right from the start. It includes everything from indian and sindhi to mexican, italian and arabic; also offers asian and exotic food items such as fondues. Has a seating area on entry and on the first floor too. Coming to my experience here, it was a mixed review since we had problems related to the air-conditioner and it's management. We sat on the first floor and there's a staircase to reach there. Ambience at both the levels is great and superb!! While the ambience was great, the air-conditioner was equally unrewarding since they weren't working properly. We even reported that to the staff but they said that they already know it's not working and started pretending that they've called the technicians at 4 in the evening the same day!! So even after coming through such scorching heat outside, the inside wasn't much different. Finally after shifting places thrice, we found a spot where cool air could be felt! Apart from all this the food was sooo yummy, fresh and adequate in quantity that my brain didn't have any other issue to focus on!🙌
Food review-
1.Cream of Tomato with Basil soup- 5/5 for quantity, 5/5 for taste. Also they serve extra croutons if asked for!!🤭
2. Pahadi paneer tikka- 5/5 for quantity, 5/5 for taste. The paneer pieces were soooo soft and felt really fresh!!
3. Lasagne Ala Napolitano- 3/5 for quantity, 4/5 for taste. Was less in quantity as compared to other places i've had lasagne. Less cheesy as per the standard flavour of lasagne.
4. Dum aloo punjabi- 10/5 for quantity, 10/5 for taste. Reallly reallly very goood in everythinggg from quantity to taste to the dum aloo pieces. Usually 1 potato is provided but here 2 were provided and it's masala and gravy was also soo yummm!!!😋
5. Butter kulcha- 5/5 for taste. Soft, fresshhhh and buttery!!
6. Chinese sizzler- 1/5 for quantity and 1/5 for taste. Typically a chinese sizzler consists of rice, noodles, manchurian balls, chinese gravy and sautéd veggies. But this consisted just of rice, noodles and sautéd veggies. There were no manchurian balls nor there was any gravy which adds to the taste in sizzlers. REALLY A BIG WASTE OF MONEY, I WOULDN'T RECOMMEND YOU TO ORDER ANY SIZZLER AFTER TRYING THIS ONE AS THIS WAS OVERPRICED AS COMPARED TO ANY OTHER PLACE.
7. Basil Citrus Breeze Margarita- 5/5 for look, 3/5 for taste. Looks too fancy and delicious but is just okay. Full of ice and  essence. Won't matter if you don't try this.

featured_reviews.name: Hitesh Harisinghani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Newly opened restaurant with another branch in Goregaon east.

The interiors are beautifully done, with Marathi songs playing in the background, adds to the authentic vibe. A special mention to Abhishek Prabhu, the manager, who was extremely helpful and guided us through the menu.

We were welcomed with papads served alongside three sides – thecha, green chutney, and masala oil – all packed with flavour.

The Pomfret in Banana Leaf was a highlight: steamed in green masala and then finished in a banana leaf. The fish was fresh and tasted amazing, especially when paired with the masala oil.

We also tried the Mutton Kolhapuri Thali, which came with pandra rassa, tambda rassa, kheema, and Kolhapuri gravy, along with bhakri, masala bhaat, and salad. A hearty and satisfying meal.

Although we initially skipped dessert, Abhishek insisted we try their freshly made in-house ice creams in jackfruit, guava, and coconut jaggery flavours — and they were absolutely out of this world! To our surprise, he didn’t even charge us for them despite our insistence.

We paid around ₹2000 for two people. It’s slightly on the higher side, but the food, service, and overall experience made it worth it. Definitely visiting again!

featured_reviews.name: Vivian Nguyen
featured_reviews.review_text:
My Marathi friend recommended me to come here and oh my… it was insanity. I already came in not hungry, but I cleared everything. After the meal, even though I was so full, I was still missing the taste of the meal I just had. On my walk back, I could taste the breath of the best meal I’ve ever had in India (& I’ve had a lot of dishes) I didn’t want to brush my teeth so I could savor the taste (but I did brush my teeth)

When I arrived, the owner told me (not verbatim), “Apologies for the smoke, because of the gas shortage, we are using coal fire to cook.” It’s a terrible situation, for sure; a lot of restaurants have been suffering from the gas shortage… but I guiltily admit I was even more excited to try the food because nothing elevates a dish more than the taste a coal brings.

The ice cream was next level, too. All made in house, real fruit, no preservatives. Left to right: coconut jaggery, guava, custard apple, and they were all amazing.

A lot of times in India, restaurants/accommodations will ask me to write a good review for them. This is 100% an organic review, unprompted. I just needed to tell the world how good this mutton thali was!!

The service was kind, attentive, and exceptional on top of everything out. I’m flying out of India on Sunday, and I am already grieving the loss of access to one of the most delicious meals I’ve ever eaten.

The benne dosa stood out with its crispy texture and buttery flavour, while the idli was soft and fresh. The cheese pav bhaji and mushroom sukha combo added a nice desi touch to the meal. The mango milkshake and mango sheera were rich, sweet, and perfect to end on a high note.

Absolutely loved my experience at muttuswami Khar🌟
Started with the refreshing Kala Khatta and Aam Panna coolers — both were perfect for the Mumbai heat. The Ghee Podi Idli was super soft and flavourful, while the Masala Benne Dosa was buttery, crisp and delicious. For mains, the Ghee Roast Mushroom with Appam and Chettinad Biryani were packed with authentic flavours and tasted amazing. Ended the meal with Payasam and Vanilla Gelato which made for the perfect dessert combo. Great food, comforting flavours and an overall amazing dining experience. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Mahima Pal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited the Khar outlet recently and absolutely loved the whole experience 🫶🏻

The café has such a warm and cozy vibe with a perfect blend of authentic South Indian flavours and modern café aesthetics. Every dish felt comforting, flavourful, and beautifully prepared.

We started with the Cheese Onion Uttappa which was soft, perfectly cooked, and loaded with cheese without overpowering the authentic taste. The Mutuswami Special Benne Dosa with paneer was honestly one of the highlights 🤤 crispy on the outside, buttery, rich, and filled generously with flavourful paneer stuffing.

The Ghee Roast Mushroom with Appam was another standout dish. The appams were soft and fluffy while the mushroom preparation had a beautiful spicy South Indian flavour that paired so well together. We also tried the Paneer Cheese Grilled Sandwich which was super cheesy, crisp, and comforting.

For drinks, the Chikoo Milkshake was thick, creamy, and refreshing, while the Kala Khatta Cooler from their summer specials was tangy, nostalgic, and perfect for the Mumbai heat.
Ended the meal with Mango Sheera and it was the sweetest ending possible 🤌🏻 warm, rich, and full of mango flavour without being overly sweet.

Loved the quality, presentation, ambience, and overall experience. Definitely a place I’d love visiting again for comforting South Indian food with a modern twist.

I went to Muttuswami Café with my skeptical, firang partner. He loved it, and so did I.

We had the Muttuswamy Special Benne Dosa, which is a mix of Benne Dosa, Masala Dosa and Ghee Podi Dosa. We also had Idli Vada Rasam, Plain and Hazelnut Filter Coffee, and a Pineapple Sheera to top it off. All of it was delicious, as well as pleasing to the eye!

The restaurant has been done up beautifully - it feels like you're walking into another world. It's super clean, and all the little touches - from the dabbara set for the filter coffee, to the paan box for the mukhwaas - serve to further elevate the experience.

Special thanks to Gaurav for being so patient and helpful.

I only dock one star because the AC wasn't working, and it's upwards of 35 degrees C right now. But honestly, the food was worth it.

10/10, would recommend!

featured_reviews.name: Hania
featured_reviews.review_text:
Peach Ice Tea
Peach Iced Tea is a refreshing burst of flavor in every sip.

Kalimiri Cheddar Broccoli
From the moment the dish arrives, the vibrant green of the broccoli is contrasted beautifully by the creamy richness of the cheddar cheese, infused with the subtle yet captivating warmth of kalimiri (black pepper). The aroma is inviting—cheesy, slightly spicy, and earthy.The broccoli retains a nice crunch, providing a fresh, earthy base to the dish. The cheddar is indulgently smooth, delivering a familiar, comforting creaminess. But what sets this dish apart is the kalimiri. The black pepper’s spice gently lingers, balancing the richness of the cheese with a subtle heat. The tender yet slightly crisp broccoli pairs wonderfully with the velvety melted cheddar. Perfect for those looking for something familiar with a hint of spice. However, the spice of cardamom was overpowered and sat on tongue, so every bite was full of cardamom, which made the next dishes taste like it too.

Tiranga Kofte
Visually, the Tiranga Kofte presents itself well, with three distinct layers symbolizing the colours of the Indian flag. The presentation is appealing and sets high expectations for a flavourful experience. However, the dish's appearance slightly outweighs its taste. The kofte has a decent blend of spices, though the flavours don’t quite come together as cohesively as expected. Each layer brings something different—the green layer offers a mild herbiness, the white layer is a bit bland, and the orange section has a touch of heat. However, the balance between them feels uneven, with the spices not blending as harmoniously as they should.
Since the appetizer had cardamom hint which was overpowering, the outer layer green part of kofta also felt it had cardamom which wasn’t pleasant on tongue.

Amritsari Kulcha
The Amritsari-styled kulcha is a delightful treat. Each bite offers a perfect blend of crispy exterior and soft, flavorful interior. The traditional stuffing of spiced potatoes and herbs is well-seasoned, providing a hearty and satisfying taste

Lachha Paratha
The Lachha Paratha is a standout with its perfectly layered, crispy texture. Each bite reveals a delightful combination of flaky. Though they forgot to add butter because it was some miscommunication, It was perfect size not big not small.

Tadkewali Dal
Tadkewali Dal delivers a heartwarming, flavorful experience. The smoky aroma from the tadka (tempering) hits you immediately, preparing your senses for a rich and comforting dish. The lentils are cooked to perfection—and well-spiced. The tadka of ghee, cumin, garlic, and chilies adds depth, bringing a savory warmth to every bite. Each spoonful is a harmonious blend of velvety dal and robust, fragrant spices. It’s a perfect dish for anyone seeking bold yet balanced flavors in a simple, soul-satisfying homely meal.

Jeera rice
Jeera Rice is simplicity at its finest. The delicate aroma of cumin wafts through each grain, giving the rice a warm, earthy fragrance. The cumin seeds add a subtle crunch and a toasted, nutty flavor that complements the perfectly cooked, fluffy rice.

Halwa (Complementary)
Rich and buttery, each spoonful melts in your mouth, releasing a wave of sweetness that’s perfectly balanced with hints of cardamom. The texture is smooth yet slightly grainy, with bursts of flavor from the roasted nuts scattered throughout.

Hospitality
The hospitality at this restaurant is exceptional. From the moment we walked in, the staff was warm, attentive, and welcoming. They ensured every detail was taken care of, making us feel comfortable and valued throughout the meal. Service was prompt, yet never rushed, with the team showing genuine care in their recommendations and interactions. Their professionalism, combined with friendly smiles, truly elevated our experience. Ashish and Prasad served great hospitality to us.

Ambience
The ambience of Rasoi strikes the perfect balance between luxury and comfort. The decor is elegant yet welcoming, with soft lighting and tasteful accents that create a warm, inviting atmosphere

This place by the Bawa Hotels Group is a good option if you’re in the mood for Punjabi food, just don’t walk in expecting completely authentic flavours. The taste is slightly toned down, but if you set your expectations right, you’ll actually enjoy the food.

The menu is quite well done, and the meal box options are a big plus. Makes ordering super easy without having to overthink or pick too many individual items.

Their parathas are definitely worth trying—served nicely with curd. Do ask for white butter separately though, as it’s not given by default and really makes a difference. The lassi is a must-have here, easily one of the better things on the menu.

Also, a special mention for the Kalimiri chicken shorba. It’s not on the menu, but if they have it, don’t miss it—it’s genuinely very good.

Ambience is nice and comfortable, so no complaints there. Service, however, is quite slow and needs serious improvement, which can get a bit frustrating.

Parking is another issue—since it’s close to the railway station, the area is always crowded and finding a spot is tough. Better to plan that in advance.

Overall, a good place to chill and enjoy a meal, as long as you’re okay overlooking the service and parking hassles.

featured_reviews.name: Suhani Mendonsa
featured_reviews.review_text:

My absolute favourites were their creamy butter chicken, soft and flavourful chhole kulcha, and the super refreshing lassi that perfectly balanced the spices. Every dish tasted like it was made with love and tradition. If you’re craving authentic Punjabi flavours with a celebratory twist, this is the place to be — go check it out and treat yourself to a hearty, happy meal!

featured_reviews.name: Jawahar Hingorani
featured_reviews.review_text:
I only gave 4 for atmosphere because there was no 4.5 or 4.75…and I got bitten by mosquitoes! The food was on point - I ordered Ajwaini Rawas for my appetizer and it came with this spicy tandoori salad (think Thai Som Yum but not as sweet or wet) and Green chutney which was the perfect accompaniment. For my mains I got the Mutton Beliram (don’t why it’s called that) which was nice and spicy, along with a roomali roti. I’d recommend ordering a naan instead - lots of very moorish sauce to lap up! Got some Jal Jeera with soda to wash it down (not sure about the boondi). Finished off with some Gulabjamun - there is definitely a hint of “Gulab” there! And just look at those soft, pillowy, inviting mounds. 😆

Overall Bawa Kitchen echoes the punjabi ethos when it comes to food. It’s definitely a place I’d recommend and visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Vijita Sonawane
featured_reviews.review_text: The Bawa Kitchen delivered a great dining experience—pure Punjabi vibes, full balle-balle. The ambience is lively and authentic, with vibrant cut-outs and the iconic “Khatiya” as a standout photo spot. Veg and non-veg starters are well curated and set the right tone for the meal. Special mention to Rahul for being an excellent host—his food suggestions and positive approach added real value to the experience. Overall, a visit that is absolutely worth it for good food, warm hospitality, and Punjabi flair.

featured_reviews.name: Benjamin SHIH
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is my first time visiting India, and I’m so glad we found this gem. The Owner/Chef is incredibly welcoming; he personally helped us order and explained the flavors with such passion.
We are from Taiwan and have tried many top-tier Indian restaurants back home, like Saffron (番紅花), Taj (泰姬), and Mayur (馬友友). But the Gosht Lucknowi Dum Biryani here is on a whole different level. My friend even said it’s 10 times better!
• The Mutton: I’ve never had mutton this tender. It’s perfectly marinated and practically falls apart. You can really taste the "Kung Fu" the Chef puts into the slow-cooking.
• The Sauce: That rich, golden gravy isn't just a sauce; it's a concentration of slow-cooked onions and spices that melt in your mouth.
• The Pro Move: Make sure to mix in the spicy yogurt raita. It cuts through the richness and adds a whole new layer of flavor to the fragrant rice.
If you want a meal made with genuine heart and soul, this is the place. A huge thank you to the Chef for such a warm welcome to India!

featured_reviews.name: shraddha nabar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved the food at The Bombay Curry!

For the 1st time we saw a chef personally taking orders and preparing them for us. We were already in heaven. The moment came when food was served it was mind blowing.

We had chicken Angara , Chicken Malai kebab, Luckowi Murgh Makhani, Dhaniwal Korma & Hyderabadi dum biryani.
I absolutely loved the chicken angara starter. Easily one of the best, juiciest and most succulent chicken I’ve ever had. Not to forget the Hyderabad biryani and Dhaniwal Korma Soooo good!

Also had a lovely conversation with Chef Kunal Nagpal and got to know about his story and how he started the restaurant.
Food, ambience, staff-  Awesome, definitely recommended

A very popular kebab & biryani restaurant just next to Khar station West.

Service is also a bit slow as everything is freshly prepared after order is taken.

The owner is friendly & sitting at counter.

We tried chicken raezala kebabs which were fresh & tasty with tandoori rotis.
Also tried the gohst Lucknowi dum biryani which was also good but taste was not as per our expectations.
On the whole a good place to visit if in Khar area.

featured_reviews.name: Sunny Solanki
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our first meal in Mumbai turned out to be an absolute gem! 🍽️
We visited a small restaurant with a cozy sitting area that can accommodate around 10 people, but the food was truly 1001%.

We started with two types of kebabs — super tasty, juicy, and full of flavor 🤤. Then came the curry with fresh naan, and everything was prepared fresh and served hot. You can really taste the quality and effort in every bite.

Small place, big flavors! 💯
Really enjoyed our first meal in Mumbai and would definitely recommend this hidden gem to anyone looking for authentic, freshly prepared food.

featured_reviews.name: Shreeya Mehrotra
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’m a North Indian living in Mumbai, and everyone knows that Mumbai doesn’t really do good North Indian food unless it’s fancy. Most days you just adjust, but some days you really miss proper food. That’s exactly the kind of day I found Bombay Curry and honestly I’m so glad I did. This place feels so homely. It’s the kind of place you go to on a random night when you’ve had a bad day, you’re tired and you just want something that feels like home.

We ordered butter chicken, garlic naan and seekh kebab and every single thing was a straight 10/10. The butter chicken was rich and comforting, the garlic naan was soft and perfect and the seekh kebabs were juicy and full of flavour.

What makes it even more special is knowing that the chefs are from Lucknow and Rajasthan because you can genuinely taste that authenticity in the food. And the chef/owner himself was easily one of the most friendly and nicest chefs I’ve ever met. Warm, welcoming and clearly cooking with a lot of love. Bombay Curry feels like a hug on a plate.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar “Sagar Anil” A
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our experience was an 80–20 mix, but overall quite memorable. We’ve visited multiple restaurants across Mumbai and often seen chefs deeply occupied with their cooking schedules. Here, however, we met Chef Kunal Nagpal—a chef with a story, beautifully balancing restaurant management and creating magic with his food.

We reached the hotel around 3:45 PM, just before closing time, which meant our order was taken in a bit of a hurry. We patiently waited for the food, and that’s where the experience truly took a turn for the better.

We ordered Chicken Malai Tikka and Butter Chicken, and both dishes were outstanding. The masala was rich and delicious. A special recommendation: do try their Chicken Malai Tikka—it’s a must!

Overall rating: 8/10. If you’re a fan of Mughlai chicken, this restaurant is definitely worth a visit.

Chef, we wish you continued success and all the best for your future endeavours.

Thank you,
Sagar & Tejashree

Came for a quick lunch and tried the Steamed Vegan Wonton. It felt light, clean and comforting. The ambience was soft and peaceful, perfect for a midday break. Service was polite and fast. The interiors are minimal and airy. A very easy and pleasant meal.
Stopped by in the evening and had the Tofu Pepper Garlic. It felt flavourful and well balanced without being heavy. The ambience was elegant and slightly moody in a good way. Staff was attentive and courteous. The space feels open and calm. A very relaxed dinner experience.

featured_reviews.name: siya garg
featured_reviews.review_text: The outdoor garden space is absolutely beautiful. The 90-year-old mango tree is the true hero  it gives the whole place a magical charm. Outstanding Thai flavours. The curries were authentic, comforting and beautifully layered. And that mango sticky rice… unreal. Easily my favourite dessert in Mumbai right now.

featured_reviews.name: Chirag Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Went with a group of 6.

We ordered a lot of dishes and no complains.
Food was great.
Drinks are subjective - My wife didn't really enjoy her picante, I enjoyed my Negroni though.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a nice experience at Sweeney. The interiors are lovely and the place has a great vibe. The staff was warm and attentive, which always adds to the overall experience.

Some of the food items were really good while a few were just average. I also feel the mocktail menu could definitely have more variety.

Overall, it was a good experience — enjoyable for a casual outing, though not something that completely wowed me. Still worth a visit for the ambience and hospitality. ✨

featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to Malaika Arora’s newest restaurant in Khar so let me rate everything I ate at Sweeney. Goat cheese croquettes with chilli honey - Very cheesy, soft and you’ll like if you like different kinds of cheese. 9/10.
Chilli butter garlic prawns - While the flavours packed a punch, it would have been better with a thicker gravy. 7/10.
Chimichurri Prawn Risotto - Quite a unique take. The prawns were spicy and nice and the risotto paired well. 8/10.
Krawpow Chicken - Pair this with Chilli Rice. This chopped chicken gravy feels like your regular comfort Chinese food but gourmet. 8/10.
Mango Sticky Rice Creme Brulee - This is supposed to be their star dessert and it does live up. The mango quality is insanely good. 9/10.
Sweeney resembles a cozy cottage with a homegrown mango tree and dimlly lit corners. It’s got a great vibe and is a good pick for dates or girly meals. If you love Thai and European cuisines, save this spot.

featured_reviews.name: PARTH KOTECHA
featured_reviews.review_text: Came here in the evening and ordered the Khau Suey Risotto. Such a creative dish and it tasted absolutely delicious. The texture was creamy and comforting with layers of flavour in every bite. I loved how unique the concept was without losing balance. The ambience of the restaurant is chic and inviting, perfect for a calm dinner. Staff members were attentive and made us feel very comfortable. Everything from the lighting to the music added to the experience. I would definitely order this again on my next visit.

featured_reviews.name: Ushma Jasapara
featured_reviews.review_text:
The restaurant Sweeney feels as if you have entered someone's home. Very striking large mango tree courtyard as the outdoor space, inside few spaces are with chairs, few with sofas and then the staircase going upwards for more !!
Food looked good, we were able to order just 3 dishes
Crispy Lotus stem 8/10
Grilled Tofu broccoli with peanut sauce 6/10
Pesto risotto 9/10
Menu is European and Thai , with a dedicated page for their signature dishes  and Jain options!!!
I v heard names of few dishes which are worth trying next time like Feta parcel, Gnocchi, miang Kham and the famous Mango sticky rice creme bruleè (practically ordered on each table)
My review will be that i would love to be at Sweeney for its ambience on a chilled weekend with some light music playing in background and  catch up with friends whose conversations we can actually hear rather than loud music blaring these days everywhere.

featured_reviews.name: Yash Karaday
featured_reviews.review_text:
Rajasthan is a delightful restaurant for authentic Mughlai cuisine. The butter chicken is exceptional, with a rich, creamy texture and perfectly balanced spices. The tandoori dishes are smoky and grilled to perfection, while the biryani is aromatic and flavorful, making it a must-try.

Although the waiter’s name is not remembered, the staff was attentive and ensured a smooth dining experience. The ambiance complements the flavorful dishes, making it an ideal spot for a hearty Mughlai meal. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Adnan Pagarkar
featured_reviews.review_text: A restaurant which is running full for so many years must be good right. Good value for money place. Eat mughlai only. You will get flavourful masala only, little meat you have to search hard to find.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A very good restaurant in Khar west for North Indian cuisine. Visited here with a friend on a weekday.

The paneer tikka was very good and also the crispy masala roomali which was nt a part of the menu. Staff was very courteous and attentive.

featured_reviews.review_text:

In main course, we ordered chicken biryani which was apt for 3 people and veg chole masala sabzi which was also good andaapt for 2 people.

featured_reviews.name: payal rogi
featured_reviews.review_text:
The establishment is situated on the ground floor of the Ramee Hotel, adjacent to Khar Gurudwara.
The atmosphere is pleasant, and the service was prompt.
The staff demonstrated a friendly demeanor, and the food quality was commendable. The portion sizes were sufficient for 2-3 individuals per dish.
We highly recommend their Chicken Crispy and Flamingo Paneer. The naan was freshly baked and notably soft. The chicken was fresh and flavorful. The nachos were baked and fresh, complemented by a delicious salsa with avocado and a cheesy sauce.
The chicken biryani offered a perfect blend of spices and was served with raita.
While the vegetable biryani was somewhat dry, it paired well with raita.
This venue is ideal for both lunch and dinner. It is a compact space, accommodating 40-50 guests, and boasts an exceptional ambiance.
The establishment also features an excellent music playlist.
The cutlery provided was of good quality.
Separate and spacious restrooms for males and females were available, maintained with cleanliness and a pleasant fragrance.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Biryani is a favourite Indian cuisine. Its basically a perfect balance of spices & rice.
'Go Biryan' is a newly opened joint in Khar which promises to make some best "Biryani's with Dum" surely stand true here.

I called for the following items

Chicken Afgani Tikka Biryani - this had an irresistible aroma of saffron , caramelized onions and afgani chicken tikka pcs. Portion quantity is sufficient for one person and had accompaniments like laccha onions & raita. Chicken pcs were soft & tender and perfectly marinated in spices. Tasted Good

Paneer Tikka Vegetable Biryani - This smelled great when i opened the box, it had mild fragrance of indian spices (Garam masala), vegetables cooked in masala along with some pieces of paneer tikka. This also came along with Raita & onions. I found it to be on a bit oilier side.

Classic Chicken Tikka - Boneless pcs of chicken marinated in spices and cooked in a tandoor  accompanied with green chutney...It had the classic tandoori flavour which one would want in chicken tikka.

Divine Chocolate Mousse - scrumptious!!

Overall all both the biryani's were delectable and easy on my pockets!!

My only suggestion t the management - containers for raita and salad can be made more sturdier as by the time they arrive, the cardboard lid becomes too soggy and messy to handle !!

Biryani by kilo!
This place serves the best biryani in the city. They have various types of biryani from their wide spread menu. The ingredients that they use are of high quality and taste really good. The proportion of all the items used in the making is just perfect. The taste is top notch and it's totally worth the pay both quantity and quality wise. The delivery was just in time and the food was hot and tasted good. The chicken korma had a perfect blend of all the flavours and was accompanied by utle tawe Ka paratha. It was a total delight! featured_reviews.name: Sadhana Viswanadhuni
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a true Hyderabadi my search for such amazing biryani never ends! I hated mumbai for not having it here! But now I don't need to look any further😍😍😍
Biryani By Kilo's biryani are sooo hyderabadi in taste that one is definitely going to have a foodgasm!❤️
My search ends here today as now I'm gonna keep ordering from BBK to satisfy my biryani cravings 😍😍 We ordered for
Paneer Nawabi Curry ✨
A delectable paneer dish! The gravy was very smooth with the right amount of spices and softtt paneer 😍
Ulte Tawa ka Parantha ✨
It's like a thicker smaller version of rumali roti but much better than that! As we ordered the food earlier we heated it up on tawa and savoured it with the paneer curry 😍
Veg Hyderabadi Biryani ✨
A properly packed flavoured rice with amazingly marinated veggies! The masalas were right and yummm. What more?? They even serve it with SALAN like in Hyderabad!!!!! 😍😍😍💞
Veg Kathal Dum Biryani ✨ - MUST HAVE!!!!!!!
This delicacy of south is a seasonal favourite and I was very doubtful if it would match to my expectations and mind me it was way beyond that! It had the perfect taste like we get it back in south!
And it was a super hit with all my family members!
😍😍😍
The biryanis were served with
Onion and lemon salad
Salan and Raita too❤️

Coming to the packaging can you think of any other better eco friendly packaging?? To top it off they even provided us with an aanch lighting which allows one to place the pot on candle burner! Which is sure to keep the handi and rice in it warm and fresh😍😍😍

If the green dough sealing gets hard and tough to remove! Don't hesitate to take help of a knife! That part might be tricky but I think a good sealed bowl is very important for perfect biryani 😍🤤🤤

So happy to have stumbled upon this brand! Forever thankful for bringing Hyderabadi Biryani to Mumbai 😍😍😍😍😍😍😍

featured_reviews.name: Rajat Sharma

Biryani by Kilo is one of safest and trusted brand delivering quality biryanis to our doorstep.
Last Thursday we ordered some of the dishes from there. The best thing about them was they deliver biryanis in earthen pots.
Delivery was quick and on time.
The dishes we tried were :

1) Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani (5/5) : Served in a earthen pot with live heating candles. The rice was cooked well. Chicken pieces were perfectly coojed in spices. Overall the biryani was awesome.
Salan and raita was complementary with the biryani was so good.

2) Chicken Korma (5/5) : It was lil sweet as I love. Chicken cooked in thick gravy had lipsmacking flavours. It was also packed in earthern pot.

3) Ulte Tawa ka Paratha (5/5) : It was just perfect. I was trying this first time and really love it.

All the dishes were scrumptious and enough for 3 people .
Hygine and stromg packing was done to avoid spillage and contamination.
Proper safety checks were done.

They made my day, surely gonna order them again.

featured_reviews.review_text: Are you a biryani lover ? If yes then Biryani by kilo is what you should try must. featured_reviews.review_text:
Best Biryani ever! I love Biryani by Kilo. They have the longest, most flavourful rice in their Biryani. We love their Hyderabadi Biryani the most. It is spicy and made in masalas. Overall Excellent food delivery and always trustworthy for the taste and flavor. Value for money!

featured_reviews.name: RCD thefoodie
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was recently introduced to authentic Sindhi food and I have to admit it’s one of the tastiest delicacies in the list of our Indian cuisines. Not many people are fond of it, cos you hardly have restaurants serving authentic, traditional dishes. But once you get to taste the original varieties you will be highly amazed.
I had a pop up event to attend @ khar and I met some good set of foodie friends over there who were equally excited like me to try out this outlet at khar. As I regularly visit the Lower Parel outlet I was damn sure that my friends would love their food. And as expected warm welcome, fabulous staff and amazing Sindhi menu to choose from.

We ordered:
🔹Beejiya di Tikki - Unique combination of lotus stem along with potatoes tasted so good, not to forget the crispy tangy fritter of lotus stem on top adds to the crunch of this soft tikkis.Highly recommended👍
🔹Kachari- Ab Sindhi restaurant aye aur papad nahi try kiya toh kya kiya?
Well this Modak shaped yummy papad made out of soaked rice is a must try. Highly recommended 👍
🔹Sindhi Pani Puri - So the puris are not crunchy but rather khasta and believe me they literally melt in your mouth and the beautiful flavour of masaledaar aloo stuffing along with sweet and spicy chutney is too good.
🔹Chole Pattice - I wonder why I never tried this dish from their menu. It was our absolute favourite and we ordered for 2 more plates. So basically it was crunchy aloo pattice which was stuffed with spicy Chana dal and served along with perfectly cooked mildly spiced chole which balanced the flavour beautifully, accompanied with pav and green chutney to adjust the spice level as per your liking. Highly recommended 👍
🔹Sindhi Thali - The complete package😜😜
Cos you get to taste so many varieties on a go.
I personally love the combination of bhuga chawal with Sindhi curry and sai bhaji with paratha.
🔹Sev Mithai - Do not leave this place without having their master piece.. Trust me it’s one of the best loaded with ghee and mawa. Highly recommended 👍
🔹Pan Milkshake - Nice and nutty paan flavour, served absolutely chilled.

Overall my girls were super happy as they all stay nearby and thanked me for introducing” Juss by sindhful “ to them 😍

featured_reviews.name: Foodadda Mumbai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Here's an outlet for authentic sindhi food & pure vegans. Our attendant Kuldeep's service was very nice. The staff members were polite and welcoming. It's nearby by Khar station, it  hardly takes 5mins to reach. The ambience is attractive. They have two floors seating section. The wall is painted beautifully with large frame of women in beautiful Indian attire, one side of the wall is full of bronze plates hanging all over the wall and scripts in hindi language, as we go ahead the wall is fully painted it's so beautiful with floral paintings and they have wooden tables, chairs which are very comfortable to seat.

Coming to the food :

In Mocktails (PE-PE-PE) :

Paan Milkshake : This was served in a bottle. The flavour of paan was just heaven. The first sip i took made me feel so refreshed, that i completed this shake in no time.

Mango Lassi : This was also served in a bottle. A mandatory drink in summers. It was tempting and nice as always.

In Appetizers (NASTO) :

Chola Dabla : It was mixture of pav, chole and chat. It was topped with spicy chutneys and curd. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

In Main Course (KHADO) :

Peeli Dal, Bhindi Basar, Steamed Rice And Phulkas :

It was the best combo meal. The best peeli dal I have ever ate, really authentic and delicious in taste. Bhindi basar was the basic bhindi cooked with tomatoes, it also tasted delicious.

Veg Sindhi Thali :

Here before they use you provide unlimited Thali but now they have changed it & keep it as limited one. And if you want you can add Sai Bhaji or Bhuga Chawal but for this you have to pay extra. Also there is option in between 2 Phulkas or 3 Pooris. This thali is really huge. The thali contains about 12 items and each one of the dishes were incredibly delicious. It has.

Aloo Tuk (2pcs)
Sindhi Curry
Paneer Makhani
Bhee Aloo Sabzi
Sai Bhaji
Bhuga Chawal
Steam Rice
2 Phulkas and 2 Pooris
Masala Chass
Kheecha Papad
Boondi Raita
Meetha Lola

In Dessert (KUCH MEETHO) :

Singhar Ji Mithai : This one is our favourite of the lot. And we will go back here just to have this dessert. It was made of sev & milk. It had a little gulkand taste and topped with some almonds. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

Overall a good place, totally worth it. Must visit this place.

featured_reviews.name: Sonali Punjabi
featured_reviews.review_text:

The food was heavenly. It was typically like “ghar ka khaana”, served really hot and with just the right amount of spices. Oil was minimal and the food was just perfectly cooked. The staff was very helpful and courteous, the the ambiance was very very transitional. I loved every moment I spent there.

featured_reviews.name: Srishti Kadam
featured_reviews.review_text:
The outlet is located at a walking distance from Khar railway station and serves some authentic dishes from Sindhi cuisine. Restaurants serving Sindhi food are very few and this one truly shines as one of the brightest amongst them. They also have good options in North Indian and Chinese food. Ordered the following from here :

Chilli Basil Broccoli & Mushroom - Broccoli and Mushroom sauteed in flavourful gravy, it tasted amazing. Mushroom was soft and the broccoli was a bit hard, the texture contrast was pretty good. Dry gravy was spicy and brought the whole dish together..

Chilli Oyster Chicken - Chunks of tender chicken cooked in oyster sauce with lots of garlic pieces, rendering the dish spicy with just a hint of sweetness. Bell peppers added the crunch in this one and we absolutely loved the flavour of the whole thing..

Chicken Kheema Pav - Looked very mouth-watering and it did deliver in terms of flavour. The quantity was great, considering that we could have easily eaten 6 pavs with the Kheema, but our tummies gave up. It was the right amount of spicy for a Kheema and the chicken was perfectly minced. Pav was soft and the eggs added that little extra..

featured_reviews.name: Nitika Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
We started with the paani puri which was delicious to the core .Super crisp puris stuffed with aaloo & boondi served with 2 types of sweet & tangy water made of imli & mint which was simply heaven . Loved it .

Next we tried the pakwan churra chaat sev puri which had pakwan as base topped wit sev , aaloo & different chutney making it immensely tasty .
It was surprising to enjoy clean , hygenic street style food in a place like kamla mill with foot tapping music , drinks & posh crowd all at highly pocket friendly rates .

We also tried a platter of deep fried sindhi special delicacies including aaloo & arbi tuk , bheeyan ji tikki & sanna pakora . Each of them had a different texture & flavour which was one better than the other & difficult to choose the best . Sprinkled with a lot of spices the freshly ground spices added a strong punch to the starters which we all thoroughly enjoyed .

We simply couldnt resist the temptation to order the special unlimited Sindhi thaali which consisted of rose sherbat , sindhi papad , aaloo tuk , sindhi curry , sindhi mutter paneer , daran ji bhaji , steamed rice , puris & sevai kheer . Every item had an identity of its own & the use of authentic masalas added the homely feel not unlike the regular commercial food available at food courts .
We simply couldnt stop ordering the sevai kheer was it was divine & perfectly balanced in all respect .A complete meal which was simply satisfying in all respect .

Thoroughly enjoyed the entire Sindhi experience .
Daddo Suttho !!!
( means very nice in Sindhi language )

featured_reviews.name: Food Chain Mumbai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Juss by Sindhful is a restaurant which specialises in Sindhi Food as their Main Cuisine and they have got this wall:- wherein you could find most of the famous words, phrases used by Sindhis, like - Dadho Sutho (Very Good), Acho Acho (Come Come), Mathe je Sur (Headache), Charyo Safa (Mad Lad) and many other Sindhi words/phrases, +1 for the quirky ambience.

It's quiet a cozy place and it boasts to be the first restaurant in India to serve unlimited Sindhi thali.

Anyway, let's start about food:-

Recommendations-

• Chole Pattice
• From Thali - Puri with Bhindi Basar, Alu Tuk, Pakoras, Sindhi Kadi with Rice
• Gulab Jamun

• Chole Pattice - 4/5

Heart Shaped Fried Potatoes with Channa embedded in it is served alongside Chole, Onions soaked in Chatni and 2 Luke warm pavs.

The Pattice and Chole tasted good, Pattice was not spicy as you would find the channa embedded in Pattice to be overwhelming at many places, and the Chole, too were not spicy and were rich in flavours.

I liked how they avoided making this classic sindhi dish spicy as it ruins the experience for me.

• Sindhi Unlimited Thali - 4.5/5

This Thali has all the signature sindhi dishes like; bhindi basar, sindhi kadhi, bhugga chawal, sai bhaji, alu tuk, pakoras which is served with rice and puri &/or roti along with Rose sherbet and last but not the least Gulab Jamun.

My favourite among the thali were pakoras, sindhi curry and rice, bhindi basar with puri, pakoras and Alu tuk.

Gulab Jamun served hot and it was topped with almonds. I liked it how Gulab Jamun was not too sweet as many places make the Gulab Jamun too sweet.

• Paan Milkshake & Guava Cooler - 3.5/5

Beverages at Juss are served in a glass bottle with their Branding on it.

Paan Milkshake has the refreshing flavour of Paan but it was little too sweet.

Guava Cooler was fruity and a worthy alternative to your regular Mojito because it is refreshing flavour and since it was mildly sweet, it was a perfect beverage to sip on during the meal.

If you are looking for that authentic Mumbai seafood vibe, Jai Jawan in Bandra is pure bliss. Here is a breakdown of a legendary meal:

The Star: Fried Fish with Pav

The Fried Fish here is iconic—perfectly seasoned, crispy on the outside, and flaky within. But the real game-changer is pairing it with the Mumbai Pav. There is something about the texture and flavor of a local Mumbai pav that just hits differently; it’s the ultimate vessel for the spicy fish, especially when you load it up with their signature green chutney and crunchy onions. It’s a simple combination, but it's a "Mumbaikar" soul-food experience

The Sides & Mains
• Prawns Crispy: These lived up to the name. Golden, crunchy, and packed with flavor, they are the perfect appetizer to snack on while you soak in the Bandra energy

• Chicken Tawa Biryani: To wrap things up, the Chicken Tawa Biryani is a must-try. Unlike traditional dum biryanis, the tawa style gives it a unique, rustic smoky flavor and a spice profile that is bold and satisfying.

The Verdict
Eating here isn't just about the food; it's about the "Bliss of Taste." If you want to eat like a true Mumbaikar, grabbing a plate of fish and pav at Jai Jawan is an absolute rite of passage.

Highly Recommended for: Seafood lovers and anyone craving an authentic taste of Mumbai’s street-side culinary excellence.

Small sitting but service is super fast and turn around table is that like always waiting customers in big rush.

All the best team JJ.

Regards!
CSD

featured_reviews.name: Prakash Dhalwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Jawan never disappoints! Tried the butter chicken, fish tikka, paneer makhanwala, roti and naan — and every dish was a winner.

The butter chicken was absolutely amazing — full of flavour with the perfect spice level. The paneer makhanwala was equally impressive, with the softest paneer I've had in a while. But the real standout was the fish tikka — completely boneless and one of the best tikkas I've ever tasted!

A few things to keep in mind before you visit: there's no parking in the area, so plan your commute accordingly. They have both AC and non-AC seating, and during peak hours you may wait up to 15–20 mins for a table — but honestly, the food is well worth it!

Highly recommend for anyone craving authentic Indian flavours. Will definitely be back! 🙌

featured_reviews.name: Pinkesh Kamwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Jawan has been one of my favourite places in Bandra for years, and it continues to deliver every single time.

The Prawns Punjabi Fry is an absolute standout — juicy, flavourful, and cooked perfectly. It’s one of those dishes that keeps bringing you back.

The Seekh Kebabs have been consistently top-notch for over two decades, which is a testament to the kitchen’s consistency and quality.

And then comes the Butter Chicken — rich, indulgent, and simply outstanding. Easily among the best I’ve had.

What I appreciate most is that despite its popularity over the years, the food quality has remained remarkably consistent.

For me, it’s hard to think of a better place in Bandra for non-vegetarian food. If you’re a meat lover, Jai Jawan is a place you simply shouldn’t miss. 👍🍗🦐🔥

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Londhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Jawan, Bandra

I recently visited Jai Jawan with my friends after a movie, mainly because we had seen and heard a lot about the place through Instagram reels. Since we were already in Bandra, we decided to give it a try. We reached the restaurant around 9:00 PM, which is peak dinner time, and had to wait for nearly 20 minutes to get a table for four—which was understandable considering the rush.

Once seated, we ordered Chicken Tikka Masala and Chicken Tandoori as starters. The starters were okayish in taste, nothing impressive. I assume this might have been due to the restaurant working at full capacity during peak hours.

For the main course, we ordered Butter Chicken with Rumali Rotis. Unfortunately, this was the biggest disappointment of the night. I’ve had butter chicken at countless restaurants, and honestly, this was the worst butter chicken I’ve had so far—lacking flavor, richness, and balance. We also ordered Chicken Fried Rice, which again was just average.

The service experience further added to the disappointment. There was a shortage of waiters, resulting in long waiting times for food. The staff seemed extremely busy and didn’t really have the time to listen properly to customer requests or feedback.

Another thing that stood out negatively was the entertainment setup. The restaurant has two large TV screens, but they were continuously playing the same 5-minute loop video of a Japanese city. On that particular day, there was an India cricket match, and playing it on at least one screen would have kept customers engaged—especially since food service was delayed.

Overall, I personally regret choosing Jai Jawan that night and feel I could have had a better experience elsewhere. This is purely my personal opinion. You may still try it once to form your own view, but my experience was not a good one.

featured_reviews.name: Dharmesh Dulera
featured_reviews.review_text:
The freshness of the seafood here is immediately evident. Every dish feels like it has come straight from the ocean to your plate, bursting with natural flavor. The fish is perfectly cooked—tender, juicy, and never overdone—while the prawns are plump, succulent, and seasoned to perfection. Their signature preparations strike a beautiful balance between bold coastal spices and authentic home-style cooking, making each bite deeply satisfying.

What truly sets Jai Jawan apart is its consistency and authenticity. There’s no unnecessary fuss or overcomplication—just honest, well-executed dishes that showcase the richness of Mumbai’s coastal cuisine. The masalas are aromatic without being overpowering, allowing the seafood to remain the star of the show.

The service is quick, efficient, and warm, adding to the overall comfort of the dining experience. It’s the kind of place where you can relax, dig in, and leave completely content.

Whether you’re a hardcore seafood lover or simply looking to explore Mumbai’s culinary treasures, Jai Jawan is a must-visit. It’s not just a meal—it’s a celebration of fresh flavors, tradition, and the simple joy of eating great food.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointing for a Place Known for Biryani

I visited this restaurant with high expectations because it’s known for its biryani, but unfortunately the experience was a big letdown.

We ordered:
Malai Tikka
Lollipop Masala
Large Chicken Dum Biryani

The Lollipop Masala was the only item that stood out. It was flavorful, almost like a Schezwan-style lollipop, and honestly the best part of the entire meal.

The Malai Tikka, however, was very disappointing. The chicken was rubbery, didn’t taste fresh, and despite decent presentation, the flavor and texture were not enjoyable at all.

Now coming to the main attraction - the Large Chicken Dum Biryani (around ₹600). For this price, getting only 3 pieces of chicken already felt underwhelming. The rice lacked the rich aroma and layered spices that you expect from a good dum biryani. There was barely any biryani masala, and while the chicken was technically well-cooked in dum style, it had very little flavor.

Overall, the biryani felt plain, dull, and nowhere close to what a place with “Biryani” in its name should serve.

What made it even more disappointing was that friends who had visited earlier said the food used to be much better - but this time none of us enjoyed it.

Final verdict:
For a restaurant called Biryani Darbar, the biryani does not live up to the name at all. I’m giving 2 stars only because of the Lollipop Masala. Everything else was far below expectations.

I really hope they improve the consistency and quality because right now, it does not justify the price or reputation.

featured_reviews.name: Suketu CHANDAN
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Biryani Darbar and it was an absolute delight!

Biryani here is easily one of the best I've had in Mumbai. Perfectly cooked long-grain rice, perfect vegetable masala and that rich, fragrant dum-cooked flavor with just the right balance of spicey, not too oily, not too dry, just perfect. The raita and salan that came with it were excellent accompaniments.

For desserts, I tried both Gajar Halwa and Shahi Tukda, and both were outstanding!
The Gajar Halwa was rich, moist, and packed with the natural sweetness of carrots, loaded with ghee, nuts, and khoya. It tasted completely homemade – warm, comforting, and indulgent.

Shahi Tukda was equally impressive – crispy fried bread soaked in fragrant saffron milk, topped with nuts and a touch of rose water. It had the perfect texture contrast and wasn't overly sweet. Both desserts felt luxurious and authentic.
The service was quick and friendly, and the portions were generous. Ambiance is simple but comfortable – perfect for a hearty meal with family or friends.

If you're a biryani lover or craving proper Mughlai desserts, Biryani Darbar Goregaon is a must-visit. Everything we ordered was top-notch. Easily one of the best biryani places in the area.

Highly recommended – 5 Stars! 🔥
Will definitely be going back soon.

featured_reviews.name: Asad Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Having always wanted to visit Lucky Restaurant, the legendary Bandra West institution famous for a Biryani so iconic it is famously loved by actor Salman Khan’s family, I was thrilled to try their brand-new branch in Goregaon East.
We started with the Chicken Manchow Soup, which was served remarkably hot and tasted fantastic with a rich, delicious, masala-based flavor, though a few unblended chunks occasionally disrupted the texture. Unfortunately, the Prawns Chilly starter was a letdown, featuring tiny, chewy prawns and an average sauce that we ultimately couldn't finish.
However, the highly anticipated Chicken Biryani completely redeemed the meal. It was absolutely perfect, boasting a flawless blend of spices, tender meat, and a delicious accompanying raita that made the whole visit worthwhile. We wrapped up with the Apricot Delight dessert, which was spectacularly flavorful and highly recommended.
Across the board, the portions were much larger than expected, justifying the slightly expensive pricing, and the service from the super nice staff was excellent. My only critique is that they should expand their soft drink menu beyond standard Pepsi and Coca-Cola to include options like Campa, Big Cola, and Lahori to better complement their heavy, flavorful dishes.

featured_reviews.name: bhushan bowlekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Paying ₹710 for this oily, pathetic dish is honestly shocking.

Ordered Lollipop Khepsa from Lucky Restaurant today, and honestly, it was one of the worst food experiences I've had.
The dish was drowning in oil. My hands were literally covered with oil while eating, and even my throat got irritated afterward.
When I called the restaurant, instead of taking responsibility, they simply said, "Utna to hota hi hai" and started giving excuses.
This is not Khepsa — it's just oily fried rice loaded with excessive oil. The quality was terrible, the taste was disappointing, and the amount of oil used was ridiculous.
Extremely frustrated and disappointed. If this is the standard of food being served, customers deserve much better. Not recommended at all.

featured_reviews.name: Iqra Memon
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience at Lucky Restaurant. The food was not up to the mark. We ordered Chicken Tikka, but the gravy served did not seem like Chicken Tikka at all. When we brought this to the staff's attention, they agreed to change it and suggested that we try Chicken Matka instead. However, it appeared that they simply reheated the same gravy, added some butter on top, and served it again.
The service was equally disappointing. We requested a tissue refill four separate times, but no one seemed concerned enough to attend to it. The staff appeared inactive and inattentive throughout our visit.
Overall, both the food quality and service fell far below expectations. I hope the management takes customer feedback seriously and works on improving these aspects.

featured_reviews.name: vishal sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently dined at Lucky Restaurant and it turned out to be a delightful culinary experience.

We ordered the half Murg Mussallam, which came with two rich and flavorful gravies – one a vibrant yellow and the other a deep red. The dish was generously topped with juicy tandoori chicken pieces, making it both unique and hearty. Paired with butter garlic naan, the meal was absolutely satisfying and more than enough for two people.

For dessert, we tried the Arabian pudding, which was a real highlight – rich, creamy, and beautifully balanced in flavor. The caramel custard was just as expected – smooth and classic, a comforting end to the meal.

The service was prompt and courteous, and the prices were reasonable for the quality and portion size. A special shoutout to the kitchen for the thoughtful preparation and presentation.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for flavorful Non veg Indian dishes and comforting desserts in a relaxed setting.

featured_reviews.name: minakshi sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
We have been regular customers of Lucky and have always trusted the quality of your food. However, our experience on 3rd January 2026 was extremely disappointing and concerning.

We ordered 1 kg Chicken Biryani, which was delivered hot and consumed immediately. Within two hours, the remaining biryani developed a strong foul smell, and all of us suffered from stomach issues afterward. This clearly indicates a serious lapse in food quality and hygiene, which is unacceptable.

This is the first time we have faced such an issue with Lucky, but it has significantly affected our trust. Serving food that can cause health issues is a serious matter and must be addressed urgently.

I request you to investigate this incident, take strict corrective action, and ensure such negligence does not happen again. I also expect an appropriate response from your side regarding this matter

featured_reviews.name: Ap Consultants
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best mutton biryani in Mumbai. The mutton pieces are soft and delicate along with a piece of potato which makes the biryani all the more interesting and scrumptious. It's has always been my all time favourite.
When I can't visit the restaurant I order it from Swiggy/Zomato.
Must try for every biryani lover.

featured_reviews.name: Suyash Karangutkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our recent visit to Lucky Biryani turned out to be a delicious journey through rich Mughlai flavours, ending with some comforting desserts that rounded off the meal perfectly.

We ordered the Murg Musallam, and it was easily the highlight of our meal. A whole chicken, richly marinated and cooked in a thick, aromatic gravy made with a blend of spices, nuts, and cream – the dish was indulgent, flavorful, and felt true to its royal roots. The chicken was tender, infused with spices, and the gravy was luscious without being overly heavy. The quantity was more than sufficient for two to three people and extremely filling, making it great value for money.

To go along with it, we had Butter Garlic Naan – soft, perfectly cooked with a generous brush of butter and a strong hit of garlic that paired beautifully with the Musallam.

For dessert, we tried the Arabian Pudding, a milk-based sweet that was delicate and smooth, with hints of cardamom and saffron. It was light and refreshing after the rich main course.

We also had the Caramel Custard, which was classic and well-done – creamy, just the right amount of sweetness, and topped with a golden layer of caramel that melted on the tongue.

Overall, Lucky Biryani delivered a satisfying meal – flavour-packed, generously portioned, and rounded off with nostalgic desserts. A great spot if you’re in the mood for classic Mughlai fare done right.

The restaurant also appeared poorly managed, with delays, lack of coordination among staff, and a noticeable drop in cleanliness standards.
It is very unfortunate to see a place that once maintained such good standards now failing to meet even basic customer expectations. I genuinely hope the management takes customer feedback seriously and works towards improving their service and quality.
